$comment: Shared Assist-wire conformance vectors. EVERY client implementation must run these and agree. Do not edit a case to make a client pass — a disagreement here is a client that will mis-handle a real gate response.
routeComment: The wire these vectors bind, as DATA — the gate (scripts/check-assist-wire-served.mjs) reads THIS field, not prose; DR-007 recorded the route as a declared gap until the spec served it; DR-023 closed that gap and the spec now serves it.

requires.$comment: Non-vacuity floor, asserted by each client's test before the cases run. Without it a client that returns DENY unconditionally passes every deny case and the suite proves nothing. KEPT CURRENT: check-assist-conformance.mjs fails when the file holds more than minCases + 4 cases, so a floor cannot lag far enough behind for a deleted vector to fail nothing.

cases.why: the only shape that may proceed with no further action
a newer server adding a field must not break an older client

reasons is genuinely optional on an allow; absence is not an error. Carries the served envelope fields (requestId may be null, timestamp) so the tolerance is proven against the real shape, not a hand-trimmed one
any 2xx is a completed request, not only 200
not a refusal, but NOT proceedable either — the challenge is unanswered

the served /api/v1/authorize contract (lib/api-spec/v1-openapi.yaml AssistResult) declares no obligations field; a step_up with none stated must parse as step_up with an EMPTY obligations list (expectObligations, asserted by every client) and must NOT proceed — absent is not-stated, never nothing-required

obligations present but not a list is a malformed body, and malformed is DENY — the same rule `assist` already gets (present-but-wrong-type denies). An earlier version of this case expected step_up, which pinned an asymmetry: a wrong-typed assist denied while a wrong-typed obligations was quietly coerced to empty and let the step_up stand with its obligations silently dropped. Both clients are now strict on obligations.
a reduced capability ceiling, not a denial

Assist is not assist; JSON keys are case sensitive

decisionId is REQUIRED by the served contract (AssistResult required: [assist, decisionId]) and every real decision carries one, because every real decision is persisted and audited under it. An allow with no id is a response nobody recorded: deny. This exact body was allow-no-reasons until the rule landed
JSON null is not an id; one client read it as the text "null" and let the allow stand
a blank id correlates with nothing
the contract types decisionId as a string; two clients stringified 42 into an id
present, wrong type

the step-up ceremony is keyed on the decision (POST /v1/decisions/{id}/step-up/challenge); a step_up with no id cannot be answered and is not a decision anybody recorded. Every outcome needs the id, not only allow
a null id read as text would send the worker to challenge decision "null"
restrict still proceeds, under a ceiling; a proceed with no recorded decision behind it is an unauditable grant

the id check runs on every outcome, so an explicit deny without a usable id is reported as an unrecorded body (the explanation names decisionId) rather than relayed as a recorded decision; without this case a client that skips the check for deny passes every vector
a deny keeps the id it can read, for correlation (missing-assist pins dec_3); a JSON null is not one, and must be carried as absent, never as the text "null"

reasons is declared an array of strings. Present-but-wrong-type is malformed and malformed is DENY, the rule assist and obligations already get; reading it as absent let the allow stand on a body this client does not understand
a non-string entry is a type violation, not an entry to drop quietly
present-and-null is present-and-wrong-type, as obligations: null already is
the type rule holds for every outcome: a restrict is a grant under a ceiling
dropping a non-string entry silently drops an obligation, the asymmetry step-up-obligations-wrong-type closed for the list itself
not JSON. A parser that keeps unquoted tokens as primitives must still not read this as the word allow; assist must be a JSON string

a repeated top-level key is ambiguous JSON. kotlinx.serialization and serde_json were measured last-wins (this read as allow before the duplicate check); Foundation's order is unspecified (measured last-wins on swift-corelibs-foundation, Darwin not measured). Any duplicate top-level key is malformed regardless: deny, and nothing is read from the body
identical values, so first-wins and last-wins both read allow: only a client that DETECTS the duplicate passes, whatever order its parser resolves in
\u0061ssist IS assist once decoded; a duplicate check that compares raw key text misses it
two ids, and no rule says which one the decision was recorded under
last-wins would drop the obligation the first copy stated
